decisions.rationale: carrier has distinct_count 16 equal to dataset.row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so the two-letter carrier code identifies exactly one row and is a defensible grain for this lookup table.
dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 against row_count 16, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is proposed.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true with no business meaning, so all three are dropped from silver.
The operator's naming convention requires code columns to carry a `_code` suffix, so the bronze 'carrier' column is renamed to carrier_code.
The bronze 'name' column is ambiguous outside the table context; the operator's convention to spell out abbreviated names motivates renaming it to carrier_name.

purpose: This table is the cleaned carrier reference lookup for the nycflights13-derived warehouse, mapping each two-letter carrier code to its full legal airline name for the 16 carriers that flew from NYC in 2013, feeding joins from flight fact tables.
usage: Join on carrier_code to enrich flight-level records with the full carrier_name; both columns are fully populated (null_rate 0.0) and carrier_code is unique per row, so it can be used directly as a join and grain key without additional filtering.
limitations: The bronze source carried only a single snapshot (_airbyte_extracted_at constant at 2026-09-02T23:26:17) with no historical versioning, so this table reflects one point-in-time capture of the carrier list and cannot be used to track carrier name changes over time; all three Airbyte metadata columns were dropped as non-business artifacts.
